preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer q (1 ≤ q ≤ 10000) representing the number of test cases.

preconditions.expression: all(len(line.split()) == 2 and all(c in '01' for c in line) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:][::2])
preconditions.description: For each test case, the first line contains two integers n and k (1 ≤ k ≤ n ≤ 10^6), and the second line contains a binary string s of length n.

preconditions.expression: all(len(s) == n for n, _, s in [(int(x) for x in line.split()) for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:][::2]])
preconditions.description: The length of the binary string s matches the given integer n for each test case.

postconditions.expression: all((stdout.strip() == 'NO') or (stdout.strip() == 'YES' and len(stdout.splitlines()) == 2 and stdout.splitlines()[1] == t) for t in [stdout.splitlines()[1] if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else None])
postconditions.description: For each test case, if no beautiful string exists, output 'NO'. Otherwise, output 'YES' followed by the lexicographically smallest beautiful string t of length k.

postconditions.expression: all(len(t) == k for t in [stdout.splitlines()[1] if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else None])
postconditions.description: The beautiful string t, if it exists, must have length exactly k.

postconditions.expression: all(all(any(a[i] == b[i] for i in range(k)) for b in [s[i:i+k] for i in range(n - k + 1)]) for t in [stdout.splitlines()[1] if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else None] for a in [t])
postconditions.description: The beautiful string t must be bit-similar to every substring of s of length k (i.e., for every such substring b, there exists at least one position i where t[i] == b[i]).

postconditions.expression: all(t == min([candidate for candidate in [''.join(map(str, bits)) for bits in product('01', repeat=k)] if all(any(a[i] == b[i] for i in range(k)) for b in [s[i:i+k] for i in range(n - k + 1)])], default='NO'), key=lambda x: x) for t in [stdout.splitlines()[1] if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else None])
postconditions.description: The beautiful string t, if it exists, must be the lexicographically smallest string satisfying the bit-similarity condition for all substrings of s of length k.
